entries.description: State a causal effect from a randomized design while retaining its identifying assumptions.
entries.notes: Report assignment, adherence, estimand, uncertainty, and assumptions relevant to the effect.
entries.template: Under the randomized design and stated assumptions, {evidence} indicates that {cause} changed {outcome} by {estimate}.
entries.title: Randomized causal effect

entries.description: State a quasi-experimental causal estimate conditional on its central identifying assumption.
entries.notes: Pair with falsification, balance, sensitivity, or design-specific diagnostic evidence.
entries.template: If {identifying_assumption} holds, {estimate} estimates the effect of {cause} on {outcome}.
entries.title: Quasi-experimental causal estimate

entries.description: Express strengthened causal credibility from independent designs or evidence streams.
entries.notes: Explain how the evidence streams carry different biases and address the named alternative.
entries.template: Across {evidence}, the causal interpretation that {cause} affects {outcome} is more credible than {alternative}.
entries.title: Convergent causal inference

entries.description: Connect an intervention, a measured mechanism, and an outcome under a causal design.
entries.notes: A mechanism measurement alone does not establish mediation; report the identifying design.
entries.template: The intervention altered {mechanism}, and {evidence} supports a resulting change in {outcome}.
entries.title: Mechanism-linked causal claim

entries.description: Compare a shared direction while preserving a meaningful magnitude difference.
entries.notes: Ensure both results use compatible outcomes, scales, and comparison groups.
entries.template: Like {source}, {finding} shows {similarity}, although the magnitude differs by {difference}.
entries.title: Compare direction and magnitude

entries.description: Identify a specific dimension on which patterns from two contexts align.
entries.notes: Do not imply broader equivalence beyond the named dimension.
entries.template: The pattern in {context_a} parallels {finding} in {context_b} with respect to {dimension}.
entries.title: Compare across contexts

entries.description: Highlight outcome agreement across a specified methodological difference.
entries.notes: Methodological diversity strengthens convergence only when biases are not shared.
entries.template: Despite using {method_difference}, both analyses produced {finding}.
entries.title: Compare methods and outcomes

entries.description: Interpret an estimate against an explicit, relevant benchmark.
entries.notes: Justify why the selected benchmark is an appropriate reference point.
entries.template: Relative to {benchmark}, {estimate} represents {comparison} for {outcome}.
entries.title: Compare with a benchmark

entries.description: State a contrast while keeping source and present-study contexts visible.
entries.notes: Follow with design or context differences that could explain the contrast.
entries.template: Whereas {source} reports {finding}, the present analysis finds {result} in {scope}.
entries.title: Contrast by context

entries.description: Contrast how one observation relates to two specified theoretical predictions.
entries.notes: State each framework's prediction before judging alignment.
entries.template: {pattern} aligns with {framework_a} but differs from the prediction of {framework_b}.
entries.title: Contrast predictions

entries.description: Report a subgroup contrast without assuming the between-group difference is tested.
entries.notes: Add a formal interaction or contrast test before claiming that effects differ.
entries.template: The estimate for {group_a} was {estimate}, while the corresponding pattern for {group_b} was {pattern}.
entries.title: Contrast subgroup estimates

entries.description: Resolve or refine an apparent disagreement by identifying a relevant distinction.
entries.notes: The distinction should change what each claim entails, not merely rename the disagreement.
entries.template: The apparent conflict between {source} and {finding} narrows once {distinction} is made explicit.
entries.title: Separate apparent contradiction

entries.description: Introduce a quantitative or qualitative result with outcome and scope attached.
entries.notes: Include units, uncertainty, and comparison basis where relevant.
entries.template: The analysis yielded {result} for {outcome} in {scope}.
entries.title: Report a measured result

entries.description: Attribute evidence and its intended proposition without adopting the source's conclusion automatically.
entries.notes: Use a precise source locator in the citation system required by the venue.
entries.template: In {source}, {evidence} is presented as evidence for {proposition}.
entries.title: Attribute source evidence

entries.description: Report a recurring empirical pattern while keeping its domain explicit.
entries.notes: Describe exceptions or heterogeneity immediately after the broad pattern when material.
entries.template: Across {scope}, the observed pattern was {pattern}.
entries.title: Present an observed pattern

entries.description: Report a point estimate together with its stated uncertainty interval.
entries.notes: Name the interval type and level in nearby text or notation.
entries.template: The estimate was {estimate}, with an uncertainty interval of {interval}.
entries.title: Introduce an uncertainty interval

entries.description: Identify a specific evidence gap without claiming that no work exists.
entries.notes: Support the gap with a transparent search or review boundary.
entries.template: The available {evidence} remains limited for {question} in {scope}.
entries.title: Bounded empirical gap

entries.description: Separate evidence for an observed pattern from uncertainty about its mechanism.
entries.notes: Do not imply that a mechanism is absent merely because it has not been established.
entries.template: Prior findings describe {pattern}, but the mechanism linking it to {outcome} remains unresolved.
entries.title: Unresolved mechanism gap

entries.description: Identify a construct or measurement dimension that current instruments underrepresent.
entries.notes: Ground the distinction between dimensions in theory or validation evidence.
entries.template: Existing measures capture {covered_dimension}, yet provide limited evidence about {missing_dimension}.
entries.title: Measurement gap

entries.description: Frame an open generalizability question as a change in a named condition.
entries.notes: Choose a condition with a reasoned basis for effect modification.
entries.template: It is not yet clear whether {finding} holds when {condition} changes.
entries.title: Boundary-condition gap

entries.description: Interpret a finding as support for a claim inside a named boundary.
entries.notes: Use indicates only when the design directly bears on the claim; otherwise select a tentative template.
entries.template: Within {scope}, {finding} indicates that {claim}.
entries.title: Bounded evidence interpretation

entries.description: Offer a tentative mechanism that could account for an observed finding.
entries.notes: Present competing mechanisms when the evidence cannot discriminate among them.
entries.template: One interpretation of {finding} is that {mechanism} may shape {outcome}.
entries.title: Mechanism-compatible interpretation

entries.description: Translate an estimate into a decision-relevant magnitude for a named stakeholder.
entries.notes: Keep the translation numerically traceable and separate it from value judgments.
entries.template: In practical terms, {estimate} corresponds to {real_world_meaning} for {stakeholder}.
entries.title: Practical magnitude interpretation

entries.description: Interpret an inconclusive result without equating non-significance with equivalence.
entries.notes: State the precision criterion or interval that leaves both possibilities open.
entries.template: Because {result} remains imprecise, the evidence does not distinguish between {possibility_a} and {possibility_b}.
entries.title: Null-compatible interpretation

entries.description: Connect a sampling boundary directly to the supported target population.
entries.notes: Avoid implying how the result would change in the excluded group without evidence.
entries.template: Because the sample excludes {excluded_group}, {finding} should be generalized only to {scope}.
entries.title: Sampling limitation

entries.description: Specify which construct dimension a measure captures and what it may miss.
entries.notes: Describe likely direction of bias only when supported.
entries.template: The measure captures {construct} through {indicator}, which may omit {uncaptured_dimension}.
entries.title: Measurement limitation

entries.description: Explain why a design cannot support causal interpretation of a finding.
entries.notes: Name the specific alternative causal pathway or bias left open.
entries.template: Since {design_feature} does not rule out {alternative}, {finding} should not be read as causal evidence.
entries.title: Design limitation on causality

entries.description: Tie limited precision to the range of interpretations still supported.
entries.notes: Report the interval or sensitivity range that motivates the statement.
entries.template: The wide uncertainty around {estimate} leaves both {interpretation_a} and {interpretation_b} compatible with {result}.
entries.title: Precision limitation

entries.description: State the central position while naming the boundary within which it applies.
entries.notes: Replace scope with a population, setting, corpus, period, or analytic boundary.
entries.template: This study argues that {claim} within {scope}.
entries.title: Direct scoped position

entries.description: Choose a bounded position after presenting a relevant empirical finding.
entries.notes: The claim must remain within what the stated finding can distinguish.
entries.template: Given {finding}, the more defensible interpretation is that {claim}.
entries.title: Position from observed result

entries.description: Locate a proposition inside a named theoretical or conceptual framework.
entries.notes: Clarify whether the framework guides interpretation or is itself being tested.
entries.template: Using {framework} as the analytic lens, we propose that {claim}.
entries.title: Theory-guided proposition

entries.description: State a position supported by multiple independent and mutually relevant lines of evidence.
entries.notes: Name the independent lines of evidence instead of using convergence as decoration.
entries.template: Taken together, {evidence} supports the position that {claim}.
entries.title: Convergent position

entries.description: Mark an interpretation as plausible while explicitly withholding certainty.
entries.notes: Keep evidence wording concrete nearby; this sentence is not a substitute for describing it.
entries.template: The available evidence, {evidence}, suggests but does not establish that {claim}.
entries.title: Confidence qualifier

entries.description: Prevent overgeneralization by naming both the supported scope and an excluded context.
entries.notes: Choose an excluded context that differs on a theoretically relevant dimension.
entries.template: This claim is limited to {scope} and may not extend to {excluded_context}.
entries.title: Boundary qualifier

entries.description: Make the premise needed for an empirical interpretation visible.
entries.notes: State a checkable condition; avoid conditions that merely restate the claim.
entries.template: If {condition} holds, {finding} is consistent with {claim}.
entries.title: Conditional interpretation

entries.description: Acknowledge a live alternative explanation when evidence is not uniquely diagnostic.
entries.notes: Use only when the alternative could plausibly generate the stated finding.
entries.template: Although {finding} supports {claim}, it remains compatible with {alternative}.
entries.title: Alternative-compatible claim

entries.description: Turn a bounded research gap into a specific, testable next study.
entries.notes: Explain how the proposed method addresses the identified limitation or gap.
entries.template: Future work should test {question} in {scope} using {method}.
entries.title: Research recommendation from gap

entries.description: Offer a reversible, conditional practice option with an explicit monitoring target.
entries.notes: Use could consider when benefits and harms remain uncertain; state trade-offs nearby.
entries.template: Given {evidence}, where {condition} applies, {stakeholder} could consider {action} while monitoring {outcome}.
entries.title: Conditional practice recommendation

entries.description: Recommend bounded implementation backed by direct evidence and a review point.
entries.notes: Assess feasibility, distributional effects, harms, and stakeholder values before use.
entries.template: Given {evidence}, implementation of {action} is warranted for {scope}, with review after {timeframe}.
entries.title: Evidence-backed implementation recommendation

entries.description: Recommend a limited next step that also reduces consequential uncertainty.
entries.notes: Prefer reversible actions when downside risk or evidential uncertainty is high.
entries.template: Until {uncertainty} is resolved, a proportionate step is to {action} and collect {evidence}.
entries.title: Decision under uncertainty

entries.description: Define the population, setting, and period covered by an analysis.
entries.notes: Use the same boundary terms consistently in methods, results, and conclusions.
entries.template: The analysis concerns {population} in {setting} during {period}.
entries.title: Population and setting scope

entries.description: Define a term operationally and name a nearby meaning that is excluded.
entries.notes: Do not present a stipulative definition as universal usage.
entries.template: Here, {term} refers specifically to {definition}, excluding {excluded_meaning}.
entries.title: Conceptual definition scope

entries.description: Set the unit of analysis and an explicit non-goal.
entries.notes: Check that later claims do not shift to a different unit without justification.
entries.template: This analysis evaluates {outcome} at the {unit} level and does not address {outside_scope}.
entries.title: Analytic boundary

entries.description: State the source type, inclusion criterion, and temporal cutoff of a review.
entries.notes: Report databases, languages, screening process, and exclusions elsewhere in the method.
entries.template: The review includes {source} that meet {criterion} and were available by {date}.
entries.title: Review inclusion boundary

entries.description: Integrate multiple independent sources around a conditional shared proposition.
entries.notes: Use plural source wording in the filled slot and identify meaningful disagreement separately.
entries.template: Across {source}, {evidence} converges on {claim}, particularly under {condition}.
entries.title: Synthesize shared proposition

entries.description: Combine sources that illuminate different parts of the same problem.
entries.notes: Explain the link between the two aspects in the next sentence.
entries.template: Together, {source_a} explains {aspect_a}, while {source_b} clarifies {aspect_b}.
entries.title: Synthesize complementary roles

entries.description: Synthesize disagreement by organizing sources around a clearly posed question.
entries.notes: Represent each position charitably and include mixed or intermediate accounts when relevant.
entries.template: The literature divides over {question}: {source_a} supports {position_a}, whereas {source_b} supports {position_b}.
entries.title: Map a structured disagreement

entries.description: Distinguish direct support from contextual material within a synthesis.
entries.notes: Explain the criteria used to rank evidential strength.
entries.template: The strongest support for {claim} comes from {evidence}, while {source} supplies contextual detail.
entries.title: Synthesize evidence hierarchy
